subject: Issues in gl2vcf() and dartR devel installation

messages.author: 44820c2887c70ec3
messages.subject: Issues in gl2vcf() and dartR devel installation
parts:
Dear team dartR,

I used dartR to (1) load a .vcf file into a genlight object; (2) subset a fraction of loci from that object using the function gl.keep.loc(), and now I would like to (3) export back that subset on a new .vcf file, using gl2vcf().

The problem is; I am getting an error message saying:
Starting gl2vcf Processing genlight object with SNP data
Starting gl2plink Processing genlight object with SNP data
Error in xx[i, ii] <- hets[ii] : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

The function gl.compliance.check() did not rise anything particular concerning my genlight object.

When trying gl2vcf() on a toy dataset from dartR (e.g., bandicoot.gl or platyplus.gl), I get something slightly different: 
Starting gl2vcf Processing genlight object with SNP data
Starting gl2plink Processing genlight object with SNP data
Error in names(x) <- value : 'names' attribute [2] must be the same length as the vector [0]

I had downloaded dartR from the CRAN a few weeks back, but the problem persists after I run gl.install.vanilla.dartR(). I am currently trying to install the devel version from Github, but for now several dependencies fail to install on my system, no matter if using the option:

gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour="dev")

or the option:

install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("SNPRelate", "qvalue"))
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR")
library(dartR)

Before I go too deep in trying to install the devel version, maybe my problem with gl2vcf() actually comes from something else? Or is it definitely an issue of dartR version?

I am running under Windows 10, with R version 4.0.4 and RStudio version 1.2.5001.

Here are my commands:
dat <- gl.read.vcf("output_msprime_0_20220125.vcf")
dat_L1000 <- gl.keep.loc(dat, loc.list = sample(dat$loc.names, 1000, replace = FALSE, prob = NULL), first = NULL, last = NULL, verbose = NULL)
gl2vcf(dat_L1000, plink_path = "C:/Users/Sidon/OneDrive/Documents/1-Post-doc_POP_SIZE/SOFTWARES/PLINK", outfile = "test.vcf"), outpath = tempdir(), snp_pos = "0", snp_chr = "0", chr_format = "character",
  pos_cM = "0", ID_dad = "0", ID_mom = "0", sex_code = "unknown", phen_value = "0", verbose = NULL)

-the vcf file is here enclosed.

Thank you very much for your help!

Best regards,
Chrys

messages.subject: Re: Issues in gl2vcf() and dartR devel installation
parts:
Hi Chrys,

Can you try the following:
1. Download the plink binary for your system from: https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/
2. Move the binary to your R working directory.
3. Grant access to the binary file using the command "chmod 755", as shown in the code below.
4. Try again running gl2vcf.

Cheers,
Luis

library(dartR)
# grant access to the binary
system(paste0("chmod 755 ",getwd(),"/plink"))
test <- gl.filter.callrate(platypus.gl,threshold = 1)
test$position <- test$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
test$chromosome <- test$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
gl2vcf(test,outpath = getwd())

messages.subject: Re: Issues in gl2vcf() and dartR devel installation
parts:
Dear Luis,

I am very sorry, but the issue persists. I really do not understand what is going on.
On my server, I have dartR version 2.0.4 on R 4.0.5, on a 64-bit Linux system.

The PLINK binaries I had installed are those from the link you gave above, and correspond to the Linux-64 system.
All permissions are set correctly. The function gl2plink() works well when launched independently (i.e., it provides .bed and .map files in my current working directory), but does not print the report either (i.e. what comes after "----------Output of function start:" -it seems like 'system_verbose' cannot work)

When launching gl2vcf(), I can see using dir(tempdir()), that the files gl_plink_temp.map and gl_plink_temp.ped were actually created. But, no .vcf output nor report after "----------Output of function start:".

The issue persists when using the platypus.gl data and using the exact same commands as given above:

test <- gl.filter.callrate(platypus.gl,threshold = 1)
test$position <- test$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
test$chromosome <- test$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
gl2vcf(test,outpath = getwd())

It seems like the function might actually be working on that Linux system, but fails to (1) print the PLINK report due to an issue with 'system_verbose" internal function and (2) store the output .vcf in the current working directory or in tempdir() where it should, contrary to gl2plink().

Did anyone else encounter such an issue when working on Linux/on a server?
If so then I guess I should get in touch with the administrators.

Please accept my apologies for all the inconvenience,
Best regards

Chrys
